results.explanation: At the declared delete-member entry, the supplied premise establishes an authenticated active ordinary non-administrator caller targeting a different active membership and successful resource resolution. The unchanged source resolves the caller and target memberships, compares targetUser.ID with currentUser.ID, and because the target is not the caller requires space administrator authority; the caller's ordinary non-administrator status therefore causes the request to be denied before the deletion effect. Source-visible authorization is deny. Separately, the accepted-policy comparison is: the original policy expects deny for removing a different active member without administrator authority, so it is satisfied; the changed policy expects allow, so it is violated. Store failure handling is downstream of this authorization gate and is not treated as authorization.

The store operation is therefore not reached on this authorization path; any source-external store failure is not authorization. Accepted-policy comparison: the source-visible deny matches the original accepted policy expectation of deny, but violates the changed/current accepted policy expectation of allow. The changed expectation for other-member is explicitly reviewed as the policy change from deny to allow. No source result is inferred from either policy text.

results.explanation: Assessment begins at the notes action entry. The supplied global add_note, view_document, and change_document permissions satisfy the declared POST permission map, and the supplied object view grant satisfies the handler's earlier owner-aware view gate. The POST then applies an owner-aware change_document gate; the supplied object change_document grant makes that gate pass whether the owner is absent or is another user, so Note.objects.create is reachable. Thus the source-visible result for the original unspecified owner-presence premise is allow. Separately, comparison with the accepted rule is satisfied: the stated global permissions are present and the object change_document grant supplies the ownership-or-grant alternative; the object view grant alone would not suffice. Note storage and later processing are effects or source-external failures, not additional authorization decisions.

condition.statement: The owner-aware check passes when the owner is absent, when the owner is the caller, or when the object permission checker grants the requested permission.

citations.quote:
def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)

Because the original premise leaves owner presence unspecified between those two cases, the source-visible result is unknown: absent yields allow and other-present yields deny. Separately, the accepted rule is satisfied on the absent-owner branch and violated on the other-present branch.
